formula/recap: Take z equals three x plus one, squared. At x equals one, the inside is four, and the local slopes three and eight multiply to twenty four. That is the slope at one point.
formula/letter: To get it at every x, keep u as a letter. The inside, three x plus one, has slope three wherever x is.
formula/outer: The outside, u squared, has slope two u. Leave it written in u.
formula/times: Multiply them: two u times three is six u.
formula/sub: Six u is still in u. Put the inside back in for u, and d z, d x is six times, three x plus one: a formula in x.
formula/check: At x equals one, the inside is four, and six times four is twenty four: the slope found before.
formula/curve: The inside need not be a line. In e to the x squared, the inside is x squared, with slope two x. The outside, e to the u, is its own derivative.
formula/curve2: Multiply, e to the u times two x, and put x squared back in for u: d z, d x is two x, e to the x squared.
worked/p1: Try one. What is the derivative of ln of two x plus three with respect to x? Call it z.
worked/in1: The inside is u equals two x plus three, with slope two.
worked/out1: The outside is ln u, whose slope is one over u.
worked/a1: Multiply: one over u, times two, is two over u. Put the inside back in for u: d z, d x is two over, two x plus three.
worked/at: Its slope at x equals one: the inside is five, so two over five, zero point four.
